headlines.summary: The quarterly results are the first since Lucid CEO Silvio Napoli, who started leading the company in June, announced a restructuring plan.
headlines.article_text: Lucid Group (LCID) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Lucid missed Wall Street's expectations for earnings and revenue for the third-quarter. The EV maker also announced a $1.75 billion increase in a delayed draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the company's largest shareholder. The quarterly results are the first since Lucid CEO Silvio Napoli, who started leading the company in June, announced a restructuring plan. In this article LCID Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT This photograph shows the Lucid Motors Lucid Air electric car at the 91st edition of the International Paris Motor Show at the Porte de Versailles in Paris, Oct. 12, 2026. Ludovic Marin | AFP | Getty Images Lucid Group missed Wall Street's third-quarter expectations as the embattled electric vehicle maker continues an "operational reset" aimed at cutting costs and narrowing losses. The company on Monday also announced a $1.75 billion increase in a delayed draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the company's largest shareholder. Lucid stock fell roughly 5% in aftermarket trading. Here's how Lucid performed in the third quarter compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Loss per share: $2.74 vs. a loss of $2.28 expected Revenue: $350 million vs. $407 million expected Despite the top- and bottom-line misses, the company's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of a loss $726 million beat Wall Street's expectations of a loss of $611 million for the third quarter. Its net loss for the quarter was $830.9 million, down from a loss of $978.4 million a year earlier. Lucid's 2025 third quarter included revenue of $336.6 million, a loss of $3.31 per share and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $717.7 million. The quarterly results are the first since Lucid CEO Silvio Napoli , who started leading the company in June, announced a restructuring plan that included implementing several cost-cutting efforts and delaying the company's upcoming midsize vehicle from the end of this year until the second half of next. "Our transformation is beginning to show progress. We are acting with urgency, strengthening the fundamentals and driving greater discipline, while continuing to invest in the priorities to deliver profitable long-term growth," Napoli said in a release. The company's turnaround plan includes $1.4 billion in cash flow improvements this year as well as focusing attention on a robotaxi program with Uber and Nuro, a factory that's under construction in Saudi Arabia and the midsize vehicle. Lucid said the capital from PIF is expected to give the company "additional financial flexibility as Lucid delivers on its turnaround program." It is expected to assist in funding "operations and key investments" into the fourth quarter of 2027, including the start of production for the midsize vehicle. The additional funds boost Lucid's total liquidity to $3.75 billion, up from $2 billion to end the third quarter. "We are grateful for the continued financial support from our anchor shareholder, which further energizes us to remain focused on execution and on our commitments as we build a stronger, sustainable Lucid," Napoli said. Lucid said Monday that the company expects to communicate its midterm plan and targets early next year. The EV maker in May suspended its guidance and many targets, citing new leadership and time needed to develop a turnaround plan. The company says it will streamline operations and connect teams more closely across its North American business. Pepsi lowered its 2026 earnings outlook in October as North American beverage volume fell 2% and food volume was flat in the third quarter. In this article PEP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Bottles of Pepsi are displayed in a store in New York City on March 17, 2025. Spencer Platt | Getty Images PepsiCo is cutting about 1,000 jobs across North America as the company tries to turn around lagging sales in its home market. "We have a clear ambition for PepsiCo North America: to build a stronger, more future-fit business that delivers industry-leading growth," Ram Krishnan, CEO of PepsiCo North America, wrote in a Monday letter to employees obtained by CNBC. "To do that, we need to be faster, more connected, and more capable, while continuing to invest in growth – behind our people, capabilities and brands." Over the next week, Pepsi plans to cut jobs as it says it aims to streamline its operations and better connect teams across the company's North American business. PepsiCo employs about 306,000 people worldwide, including roughly 125,000 in the United States, as of Dec. 27, according to a company filing. The Wall Street Journal first reported the coming layoffs. In October, PepsiCo cut its full-year earnings outlook, citing the struggles in its home market. During the third quarter, its North American beverage unit saw volume shrink 2%, while its North American food division reported flat volume. While the company has tried to boost sales by cutting prices and investing in marketing, the turnaround is taking longer than expected, CFO Steve Schmitt said on the company's earnings conference call. Shares of Pepsi rose slightly in afternoon trading. The stock is down nearly 1% this year, lagging behind the S&P 500 's gains of nearly 11% over the same period.
